reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it affirmatively promotes OneCoin through a cryptocurrency participation-and-returns mechanism and an invitation to join the financial movement. It also connects the system to mobile money transfers, a one-minute worldwide transfer claim, and absolute safety assertions reinforced by wallet imagery and a prominent "SAFE" visual. The title and description leave some informational or news framing possible, and the records do not establish completed transactions, losses, or the truth of the claims.

opening.argument: The material does not promise a guaranteed return. Its wording is exploratory and qualified, asking “how do we know” and describing what “may” be interesting rather than stating that viewers will profit. The narration also presents OneCoin as a proposed financial-services platform, including claims about speed, simplicity, and safety, but those claims do not themselves establish a deceptive investment solicitation. The title is framed as a basic question, “What is OneCoin?”, supporting an informational reading rather than a promise of financial gain.

Likewise, “absolutely safe” is a broad capability assertion, not proof that the video solicits an investment. The reference side itself concedes that no guaranteed outcome or precise return is established.

opening.argument: The strongest reading is an educational explainer about how a proposed cryptocurrency and its payment system are supposed to work. It explains that users need only a mobile phone, describes transfers, and discusses how cryptocurrency pricing is understood. The title asks what OneCoin is, while the description calls the material “news, articles, and videos,” which is consistent with informational coverage. The visuals are diagrammatic: they show a globe, devices connected to OneCoin, and a phone marked for payment, supporting demonstration of a claimed system rather than proof of a completed solicitation.

opening.argument: This can be understood as promotion of an ordinary digital payment service. The stated use is sending money to relatives and transferring funds, with speed, simplicity, and mobile access presented as service features. The material does not show a deposit request, credential collection, downline recruitment, completed payment, or guaranteed income. Even the purchase-related passage says only that a buyer may receive a later share of coins; it does not establish a cash return, profit, or compulsory payment. The phone, laptop, and connected-device imagery is consistent with describing a digital service.
